First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+(kx)^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(kx)+C
$$

We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{8}{1+16{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}\frac{1}{1+16{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}\frac{1}{1+(4x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x)]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4a)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(0)) \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4a).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x)=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x)=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/4daa526482964d826d5cf17a9a646de0a01059e7f886ddd1e19bcb09c4c25ee3.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{8}{1+16{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4a) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
